newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - spot stocks running low.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - spot stocks running low.

text.p: The New York physical coffee market was sluggish this week as a shortage of prompt supply put a crimp in spot market activity, traders said.
Traders said hefty differentials, coupled with the mediocre quality of many available spot beans, kept roasters on the sidelines.

Underscoring the supply woes, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported earlier this week that stocks of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses fell in September by 205,000 60-kg bags, to 1,611,000 bags, their lowest level since the GCA began keeping track of inventories in January 1988.
"There is no spot coffee to talk about," one trader said. "Roasters are only willing to pay up if they absolutely have to have to."

Traders said roasters continued to rely on shipments of Brazilian coffee, and, to a lesser extent, pricey Colombian beans. A shipment of around 60,000 bags of Colombian coffee set to arrive in New York on Saturday had been well sold in advance.
